selector.rationale: Bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, dilated fetal bladder, and oligohydramnios are consistent with Posterior Urethral Valves, which is a more specific diagnosis than Prune Belly Syndrome

rejected.label: Wunderlich syndrome
rejected.why: while the perirenal fluid collection is consistent with Wunderlich syndrome, the other findings are more consistent with a urethral obstruction

rejected.label: Ureteropelvic Junction Obstruction
rejected.why: the presence of a dilated fetal bladder and oligohydramnios suggests a more distal obstruction, such as Posterior Urethral Valves

support_spans: A left perirenal fluid collection measuring 64 × 34 mm that displaced the left kidney anteriorly; the collection contained multiple light bands, flocculent echoes, and slightly echogenic material
serum creatinine was elevated at 156.1 µmol/L, indicating impaired renal function
Magnetic resonance urography revealed bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention
